title: Partition, failover, and consistency lab
description: Choose a replica condition to trace which acknowledgements count. Node failover can preserve W=2; a network partition with only one reachable copy forces an explicit CP or AP decision.

nodes.label: Application client
nodes.detail: Sends the key, value, idempotency token, deadline, and consistency level. A retry preserves the same operation identity.

nodes.label: Request coordinator
nodes.detail: Locates the replica set, sends concurrent operations, counts valid acknowledgements, and never reports a stronger result than it collected.

nodes.label: Partition map
nodes.detail: Maps the key to one versioned replica set with a copy in zones A, B, and C. Membership changes publish a new generation.

nodes.label: Replica A
nodes.detail: Persists the mutation and version before acknowledging. It can serve as one member of a read or write quorum.

nodes.label: Replica B
nodes.detail: Holds an independent copy. A failed or isolated replica is excluded from the acknowledgement count until it responds correctly.

nodes.label: Replica C
nodes.detail: Provides the third failure-domain copy and can replace Replica B in a W=2 quorum during a single-replica failure.

nodes.label: Hint and repair
nodes.detail: Retains bounded hints and later compares versions. It restores convergence but cannot retroactively make a W=1 response strongly consistent.

nodes.label: Operation result
nodes.detail: Returns success only after the selected threshold is met, or returns a retryable quorum failure when the requested contract is impossible.

scenarios.label: Healthy W=2
scenarios.summary: All three replicas are reachable. The coordinator returns after A and B persist the write; C may complete after the user receives success.
scenarios.result: Two durable acknowledgements satisfy W=2. The third attempt may finish asynchronously, and repair covers a missed copy.

scenarios.label: Replica B down
scenarios.summary: Replica B is unavailable, but zones A and C remain reachable. The coordinator keeps the requested W=2 contract by counting different healthy replicas.
scenarios.result: The write still succeeds at W=2 through A and C. A bounded hint targets B, and anti-entropy verifies convergence after recovery.

scenarios.label: Partition: keep W=2
scenarios.summary: The coordinator can reach only Replica A. The caller requested W=2, so one acknowledgement is evidence of partial progress, not permission to report success.
scenarios.result: The coordinator returns a retryable quorum-unavailable result. Availability drops for this key range, but no W=2 write is falsely acknowledged.

scenarios.label: Partition: allow W=1
scenarios.summary: The workflow explicitly permits W=1 during isolation. Replica A accepts locally while B and C may still hold or accept another version on their side of the partition.
scenarios.result: The user receives an available but explicitly weaker success. Reads may be stale and versions may conflict until connectivity returns and domain-aware repair converges them.
